The TNF superfamily of molecules plays an essential role in tooth cusp morphogenetic signalling, and that Troy/Traf6 are essential components of a TNF pathway that regulates tooth cusp morphogenic signalling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the TNF family member Traf6 as essential for tooth cusp morphogenensis and we showed that Traf6 is a downstream effector of EDAR.
Traf6 is required for the formation of cusps in the molars and that it acts downstream of the EDAR signalling pathway in this process.
Traf6 is an important regulator of tooth morphogenesis and that the Traf6‐Troy signalling pathway may represent an alternative pathway to Eda‐EDAR signalling in tooth development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new TNF family member is expressed in tooth enamel knots and that a Traf adaptor is essential for cusp morphogenesis.
a TNF family of proteins, called the EDA pathway, is important for the development of teeth.
Traf6, which is an intracellular adaptor for the Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) related orphan receptor, Troy, is also involved in molar cusp morphogenesis.
